fullPassage:
Bull Market vs. Bear Market

Stock market movement can be divided into two major trends: bull market vs. bear market.

BULL MARKET
A bull market is a rising stock market situation in which economic conditions are favorable to investors. They include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other positive economic indicators. Think of a charging bull in a field raising its horns. In a bull market, investors often believe in the market's present and future performance. As such, they increase their stock purchases and maintain their investments.

BEAR MARKET
Like a standing bear having lowered its front legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It occurs when economic conditions are not favorable, and most stocks experience decreases in value. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment, and low wages are possible conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic situations, investors frequently have negative views of the stock market, which may lead them to sell their stocks.

questions.passage: Stock market movement can be ①<u>divided</u> into two major trends: bull market vs. bear market. A bull market is a ②<u>risen</u> stock market situation in which economic conditions are favorable to investors. They include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other ③<u>positive</u> economic indicators. Think of a ④<u>charging</u> bull in a field raising its horns.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①구분된다 ②상승하는(rising) ③긍정적인 ④돌진하는
det.analysis:
✅ ② risen → rising: 'a rising stock market situation' — 명사 situation을 수식하는 현재분사 rising(상승하는) 필요. risen은 과거분사로 보통 have와 함께 사용
❌ ①③④: 모두 적절
det.tip: rising(현재분사/형용사: 상승하는) vs risen(과거분사: have risen에서 사용)

questions.passage: Like a standing bear ①<u>has lowered</u> its front legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It ②<u>occurs</u> when economic conditions are not favorable, and most stocks ③<u>experience</u> decreases in value. In difficult economic situations, investors frequently have negative views of the stock market, ④<u>which</u> may lead them to sell their stocks.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①낮춘 채(having lowered) ②발생하다 ③경험하다 ④관계대명사
det.analysis:
✅ ① has lowered → having lowered: 분사구문에서는 'having + p.p.' 형태 사용. 'has lowered'는 완전한 동사이므로 분사구문 부적합
❌ ②③④: 모두 적절
det.tip: 분사구문 완료형: having + p.p. (has/have + p.p.는 분사구문에 쓸 수 없음)

questions.passage: A bull market is a rising stock market situation ①<u>in which</u> economic conditions are favorable to investors. They ②<u>include</u> high employment rates, GDP increases, and other positive economic indicators. In a bull market, investors often ③<u>believe</u> in the market's present and future performance. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①~에서 ②포함하다 ③믿다 ④유지한다(maintain)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ maintaining → maintain: 'increase와 and로 연결된 병렬구조' → increase(동사원형)와 같은 형태 필요
❌ ①②③: 모두 적절
det.tip: 병렬구조: they increase ~ and maintain ~ (둘 다 동사원형)

questions.passage: Like a standing bear having lowered its front legs, a bear market implies a decline in stock values. It occurs when economic conditions are not ①<u>favorable</u>, and most stocks experience decreases in value. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment, and low wages are ②<u>possibly</u> conditions for a bear market. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①유리한 ②가능한(possible) ③어려운 ④부정적인
det.analysis:
✅ ② possibly(부사) → possible(형용사): 명사 conditions를 수식하므로 형용사 possible 필요
❌ ①③④: 모두 형용사로 명사를 적절히 수식
det.tip: possible(형용사: 가능한) vs possibly(부사: 아마도) — 명사 앞에는 형용사
